(2017). The second, WINDoe (following Gebauer and Bell 2024), uses variational retrieval techniques to provide 30-minute averaged horizontal wind speed, horizontal wind direction, and relevant uncertainty estimates (Gebauer and Bell 2024) every 15 minutes on a uniform 10-m height grid. Using these unified products, full atmospheric profiles of relevant wind parameters can be examined over timescales ranging from seasonal to diurnal. For unified thermodynamic profiles across each observational site, the established TROPoe algorithm (Turner and Lohnert 2014; Turner and Blumberg 2019; Turner and Lohnert 2021) was applied across all thermodynamic profiler and surface meteorological observations collected during the field campaign. TROPoe is well established as a reliable method to derive thermodynamic profiles from ground-based remote sensing radiometers, particularly under variable atmospheric conditions (Turner 2024). BUOY OBSERVATIONS Buoy-based observations of surface winds, surface meteorology, Doppler lidars (on 2 buoys), and turbulence statistics were compiled from available onboard sensors and relayed in near-real time to shore- based servers as combined 10-min increment observations. For the DOE-lidar buoy, an onboard motion compensation system was developed to compute turbulent fluxes in near real-time (Marcial et al. 2024). Additional post-processing for turbulent fluxes for the other deployed buoy systems is underway. OCEAN SURFACE CURRENTS AND SURFACE WINDS Maps of ocean surface currents were estimated from the observations of a series of four multi-antenna HFRs [described by Kirincich et al. (2019); Kirincich and Emery (2023)] previously deployed in the region at the coastal land sites used for WFIP3 (Fig. 3). Using both radial and elliptical current returns from the fully networked HFRs, the array produces independent, 30-min averages of vector surface currents at-2 km resolution over a 150 km x 80 km area using standard methods (Kim et al. 2007; Clary et al. 2019). RMS differences of the system against in situ observations were∼7 cm s−1. High-resolution estimates of the surface wind field over the study area were also made from the HFR observations following the recent methods of Kirincich and Emery (2025). Independent from the estimated surface currents from the HFR, but at similar range and resolution, the coupled observations of winds and currents at the ocean’s surface provide a potentially powerful tool for understanding the coupled system (Fig. 3). PROJECT DATA AVAILABILITY 17 Data from all sensors, as well as the data products described above, are available for public use via a centralized project-specific download site maintained by the DOE (Krishnamurthy et al.2025).
